Payment gateway charges in India range from 1.95% to 2% for domestic transactions in 2026, but the real cost depends on payment method exclusions, credit card thresholds, success rates, and whether the gateway charges AMC or setup fees.


Multiple payment gateways in India are advertising “0% platform fees” right now. The headlines look identical. The terms behind them are not.


Every business comparing payment gateways in India eventually asks the same question: if two offers both say 0%, why would I pay more with one than the other? The answer is in what each offer actually covers, which payment methods are included, which are excluded, what technology you get access to during the promotional period, and what your real cost looks like after the offer ends. This guide breaks down what[payment gateway charges](https://razorpay.com/payment-gateway/) actually include in 2026, what “0%” means in practice, and how to choose the offer that gives your business the most value from day one.

- **At Rs. 10 lakh monthly GMV, one percentage point of payment success rate is worth Rs. 10,000 in captured revenue.** A 0.05% MDR difference at the same volume is worth Rs. 590. Success rate is roughly 17 times more valuable than headline MDR for businesses under Rs. 25 lakh monthly GMV.
- **Razorpay’s 0% offer includes the full technology stack from day one.** Smart routing, intelligent retries, 100+ payment methods,[Payment Links](https://razorpay.com/payment-links/) , Payment Pages, Invoices, card tokenization, and fraud screening are all active during the offer at no extra charge. There is no lite version during the promotional period.
- **Razorpay is the only Indian payment gateway that also offers business banking, payroll, lending, and POS under the same account.** You start with payments during the 0% offer, and the rest of the stack is there when you need it.


## What Goes Into Payment Gateway Charges: The 7 Costs That Decide the Cheapest Option


There are seven cost components in a payment gateway. Most merchants only compare the first one.


### **1. Platform Fee (MDR or TDR)**


The percentage deducted on every successful transaction. Standard domestic rates in India are 1.95% to 2% across major providers in 2026.


### **2. GST at 18%**


Applied on top of the platform fee. For example, a 2% platform fee becomes 2.36% after GST. GST is a government levy and applies to the payment gateway’s platform fee regardless of any promotional offer or discount. Always factor GST into your cost calculation when comparing payment gateways.


### **3. Setup Fee**


Some payment gateways charge Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 20,000 as a one-time onboarding cost. Razorpay charges zero.


### **4. Annual Maintenance Charge (AMC)**


Fixed yearly fee regardless of transaction volume. Some providers charge Rs. 4,999 to Rs. 9,999 per year. At Rs. 2 lakh monthly GMV, a Rs. 4,999 AMC adds 0.21% to your effective rate, enough to cancel a lower headline MDR. Razorpay charges zero AMC on every plan.


### **5. Instant Settlement Fee**


Standard settlement is T+2 working days. Razorpay offers[instant settlements starting at 0.20% to 0.30%](https://razorpay.com/capital/instant-settlements/) per transaction. Some providers charge 0.30% or higher for the same service.


### **6. Refund MDR Retention**


When you refund a customer, most payment gateways keep the fee from the original successful transaction. At a 10% refund rate on Rs. 10 lakh GMV at 2%, that is Rs. 2,000 per month in fees on revenue you returned.


### **7. Subscription and Recurring Billing Costs**


Mandate creation, debit attempt, and retry fees apply separately for SaaS and subscription businesses.

Every 0% offer in India excludes certain payment methods from the benefit. Common exclusions include Prepaid Cards, Corporate Credit Cards, AMEX, Diners Club, EMI, and international transactions. These categories are standard across most providers, including Razorpay. Transactions through excluded methods are charged at standard rates during the offer.


The real differences between 0% offers are not in the exclusion list. They are in the credit card threshold that can revoke the offer, the technology included during the promotional period, and the post-offer pricing structure. That is where this guide focuses.

### The Credit Card Threshold on the 0% Offer


Some providers revoke the 0% offer if credit card transactions exceed a certain share of your total GMV. The thresholds vary across providers. Some T&Cs set the limit at 60% of total processed volume, meaning a business where two out of three customers pay by credit card could lose the offer entirely.


Razorpay’s credit card threshold is 90%, which is generous enough that virtually no business under normal operations would trigger it.


This matters for premium D2C brands selling electronics or fashion (typically 50% to 70% credit card share), travel and hospitality companies (60% to 80%), education platforms with high-ticket courses (60% to 75%), and B2B service providers where corporate cards are standard.

## Post-Offer Pricing: What Payment Gateway Charges Look Like After 0% Expires

### The Post-Offer MDR Gap Is Smaller Than You Think


The standard domestic rate across major Indian payment gateways sits between 1.95% and 2%. At Rs. 10 lakh monthly GMV, the difference between 2% and 1.95% after GST works out to Rs. 590 per month.


Now add instant settlement to the equation. If you settle 30% of your GMV instantly:


At 0.25% (Razorpay’s midpoint): Rs. 3 lakh x 0.25% = Rs. 750 per month


At 0.30% (charged by some providers): Rs. 3 lakh x 0.30% = Rs. 900 per month


The instant settlement gap is Rs. 150 per month. Subtract that from the Rs. 590 MDR difference, and the real monthly cost gap is roughly Rs. 440. That is about Rs. 15 per day.


One additional successful payment of Rs. 5,000 in a month, captured because of better routing and retry infrastructure, covers that gap entirely.

Razorpay charges zero AMC on every plan. Some legacy payment gateways charge Rs. 4,999 to Rs. 9,999 per year in annual maintenance regardless of transaction volume. At Rs. 2 lakh monthly GMV, a Rs. 4,999 AMC adds 0.21% to your effective rate, enough to cancel out a lower headline MDR.

For businesses processing above Rs. 5 lakh per month, Razorpay offers custom enterprise pricing. The standard 2% rate is a starting point, not a ceiling. As your volume grows, you can negotiate volume-based pricing tiers that bring the effective rate down. There is no separate enterprise plan to sign up for and no minimum commitment to access the conversation. This is relevant because at higher volumes, even small MDR differences compound into large absolute numbers. At Rs. 1 crore monthly GMV, a 0.1% reduction in MDR saves Rs. 10,000 per month. Razorpay’s custom pricing is negotiated based on your transaction volume, payment method mix, average order value, and business category.

## How to Calculate the Cheapest Payment Gateway for Your Business


### **Step 1: Start with Attempted GMV**


Start with your attempted GMV, including failed checkout attempts. This is the total value of all transactions your customers try to make, not just the ones that go through.


### **Step 2: Apply the Success Rate**


Apply the success rate. A 93% rate on Rs. 10 lakh captures Rs. 9.3 lakh. An 85% rate captures Rs. 8.5 lakh. That Rs. 80,000 gap is the largest cost variable in your payment gateway decision.


### **Step 3: Calculate Transaction Fees**


Calculate fees on captured GMV. Multiply by the platform fee, then by 1.18 for GST. For example, Rs. 9.3 lakh at 2% plus GST costs Rs. 21,948 per month.


### **Step 4: Add Fixed Fees**


Add fixed fees. Divide the AMC by 12 for the monthly cost. At Rs. 2 lakh monthly GMV, a Rs. 4,999 AMC adds 0.21% to your effective rate. A gateway with zero AMC eliminates this line item entirely.


### **Step 5: Add Settlement and Refund Costs**


Add instant settlement and refund costs. If you settle 30% of Rs. 10 lakh instantly at 0.25%, that is Rs. 750 per month. Add retained MDR on refunds based on your refund rate. The gateway that leaves the highest amount in your account after this full calculation is the cheapest one for your business.
